{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish at the start of the activity, chosen because its outline reads clearly to a judge. I laid the start domino and the whole top line, about 57 dominoes, which is the stretch the fall travels along first and the one everything else hangs from. At the final check, tracing by eye, the run from the start was expected to knock over about 117 of the 119 standing dominoes. That included both tail tips, and only two stray dominoes beside the nose sat off the outline. I can't claim to know how the judge read it.

Execution: I built the top line in steady passes and carried it round the nose. I then inspected the nose area closely five times, from 2:30 to 4:30, to confirm the fall passed from the top line into the bottom line. When a small gap showed there, I delegated the join so it was closed quickly. After that I kept my hands off the table so nothing got bumped.

Collaboration: I split the work early into top line, bottom line and tail so people weren't doubling up. I pointed teammates to the specific spot at the nose that needed a join, and I gave clear status updates to the table and to the manager at each check-in. I agreed the hands-off rule with the group once the run was solid.

Leadership: I set the direction on the animal, assigned pieces, and kept the group calm and focused through the final minutes. I stayed on my own piece rather than crowding others' work, and I called the hands-off point so the table finished with a clean, intact build.", "my_share_percent": 35}
